design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing, that the care plan on her ring be ended and the unused part of the premium given back, and the figure she is owed cannot be reached without first discovering, from the published coverage rules alone, that the coverage still owes an answer on the claim standing open against her ring, answering it, and only then working the refund out on the world that answer leaves behind. Both figures are reconciled out of a twenty-six-month ledger and out of two other desks' records (the workshop's work order and the loyalty membership); neither is readable from any single field. Nothing here turns on choosing between similar tools: the two writes are the only writes the coverage rules provide for, and the whole difficulty is in knowing that the first is owed at all and in getting both numbers exactly right.

SCOPE CLAIMED AND HEADROOM (principle C). Nothing was occupied before this task. Task 0 claims protection_ext_claim_settlement (what an accepted claim draws from the benefit allowance, target tool record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c) and protection_ext_cancellation_refund (what is returned when live coverage is given up, target tool confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509). Left free for task 1, whose draw is two prerequisite problems and factor counts 6, 4 and 5: the refusal of a claim the coverage does not answer for (protection_claim_denied), the granting afresh of a coverage year's benefit allowance (protection_allowance_reinstated) and the carrying of benefit across on a transfer (protection_plan_transferred), together with the customer's own transfer confirmation. Those three are independent of everything claimed here: they compute different quantities, on different base policies, through different tools.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED. scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/protection_claims_desk --tasks 2 prints for this task {"task": 0, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/protection_claims_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}. The tree therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem, and the two computations carry five and four declared factors: protection_ext_claim_settlement takes the five, protection_ext_cancellation_refund takes the four.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: protection_ext_cancellation_refund, the problem the customer's own request points at. Prerequisite problem: protection_ext_claim_settlement. One edge, protection_ext_cancellation_refund waiting on protection_ext_claim_settlement. kind=value_input; gate=returned_share (a compute binding of the root); form=state; prerequisite sentence, quoted verbatim from the root policy's own rule: 'The premium returned is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the plan stands recorded against it.' Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is 'only after', joining the root's own result, the premium returned, to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state, a settlement entry standing against a claim reference and carrying the benefit consumed, not an action and not a performer; (3) it names no tool, no policy id and no code token; (4) its strength is the strength of the edge, 'only after' and 'every claim entered', no wider and no narrower than the condition. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: only record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c books a settlement entry carrying benefit consumed, and the derivation is prerequisite sentence plus the records (the filing entry CL-320742 of 2026-08-28 carries claim_outcome not_applicable, so no benefit stands recorded against it) plus the settlement policy's own rule (which says what an accepted claim draws and books) leading to one action, answering that claim. Resolving action: record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c, owner agent. Seed evidence that the edge is false at the opening: initial_state.protection_ledger.b803ba2d-26a7-411f-8f38-5589c47c6b87.claim_outcome = 'not_applicable', and no protection_claim_settled entry anywhere in the ledger carries claim_reference CL-320742. Topological order: protection_ext_claim_settlement, then protection_ext_cancellation_refund. There are no parallel edges to order. Deletion sensitivity, actually run: skipping the settlement write and replaying everything else leaves settlements_in_window at 0, so returned_share falls back to the whole unused premium and refund_amount moves from 246.67 to 333.06. user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: the customer says only that she wants to end the plan and get back what she has not used, and the ring's being at the workshop is given only when asked; she never mentions a claim, an outstanding item or anything needing to be sorted first. The tool layer blocks nothing: confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509 has no reference to any claim and would write a cancellation and a refund of whatever amount it is given at any time, so the consequence of skipping the settlement shows up only in the terminal hash.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Write 1, subject protection_claim_settled. Governing base policies: protection_claim_settlement, gate one_settlement_per_claim, kind dedup, 'A settlement is made only when no settlement already stands against that same claim reference.' Authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key protection_ledger.claim_reference bound to the action argument claim_reference. Evidence at frozen time: the only entry carrying CL-320742 is the filing b803ba2d-26a7-411f-8f38-5589c47c6b87 with claim_outcome not_applicable, so no settlement stands and the gate holds. protection_agg_allowance_pooling has no structured eligibility; its scope governs the write, the allowance drawn on being this plan's own and never pooled. protection_included_services has no structured eligibility; its scope governs which routine work needs no claim at all. There is no time gate on this write: protection_claim_intake's proof_of_loss_window and coverage_in_force both apply to protection_claim_filed, and the filing already stands on the record. Write 2, subject protection_plan_cancelled and protection_premium_refunded. The only governing base policy is protection_cancellation_refund, whose single gate full_refund_window is retired for this write by the declared overwrite quoting its condition sentence verbatim, so the policy governs this write by scope alone and no time gate is inherited. The boundary reasoning is kept for the record even though the gate is retired: the plan was bought on 2024-07-19 and the coverage's full-refund window is 30 calendar days from the day of purchase counted inclusively, so a cancellation reaching the desk on 2024-08-18 would have been inside it and one on 2024-08-19 outside it; at frozen time 790 days have passed, which is why the administration-fee ladder cannot take its no-fee tier.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The target of write 1 is the single claim reference CL-320742, entered on 2026-08-28 against plan da7ae772-e1c5-4d1f-8ce9-100724b6f0dc for the covered piece RING-32417 and sent to the bench on work order WO-321065. The correlation key is the claim reference itself, which ties the filing entry, the settlement that answers it (through source_entry_id = b803ba2d-26a7-411f-8f38-5589c47c6b87) and the workshop's priced lines (whose protection_claim_reference is CL-320742). Excluded by that same key: everything under CL-320411, the filing of 2025-08-21, the settlement of 2025-09-02 and the three service ledger lines on WO-320118, which belongs to the earlier loss and is already answered. The target of write 2 is the plan record itself; the premium entries that compose what the customer has paid are the receipt of 2024-07-19 and the give-back of 2024-08-06 booked against it through source_entry_id, and no other plan of this customer is in play.

FACTOR CARD, protection_ext_claim_settlement (five declared factors, exactly the count drawn). repair_figure_basis (method, cross-difficulty on service): the ladder reads the work order carrying the claim's reference; here it shows no completed date and an authorised ceiling of 1325.00, so the figure standing for the repair is that ceiling. The computation document's standard method is the labour and parts charged (640.00 + 305.00 = 945.00), which would have given 759.50. Evidence rows: initial_state.service_orders.3e2059dd-ed38-4f09-abca-627a3ca8d129 (completed_date empty, authorized_total 1325.00, estimated_total 1180.00) and the two priced lines 76fc26f2-acba-4d95-abe3-40fa385cf3f4 and 3e0998a9-1f3d-4304-8110-375a9d5fd228. loyalty_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty on circle): the membership 32f6b476-0c94-4d96-a163-5560ab71dd60 stands active with qualifying spend since the tier took effect of 8420.00 against the Gold tier's maintenance figure of 5000.00, so the whole of the Master Jeweler Service loyalty discount of 5 per cent comes off; the baseline takes nothing off and would have given 1120.95. wear_reduction_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty on service): the most recent inspection entry 5469e853-4b70-4472-96b6-312b0204e33c of 2026-05-12 records 'pass' and the work order records no rework, so the annual reduction is taken at the sound-piece share, 3.0 per cent a year rather than the published 6.0; the baseline would have given 996.93. answered_share (parameter, cross-difficulty on service): the Master Jeweler Service level targets 10 business days against the coverage's own target of 12 and the coverage offers expedited handling, so the coverage answers for the expedited-level share, 0.9; the baseline answers for all of it and would have given 1183.22. deductible_borne_by_customer (parameter): no settlement entry falls inside the twelve-month window, because the earlier settlement 4fd363f0-2127-491f-8b09-3142640019b7 of 2025-09-02 is exactly twelve whole months back and therefore outside it, which is the near-miss record of this task, and the most recent inspection is four whole months old against a six-month interval, so nothing is charged to the customer; the baseline charges the published 50.00 and would have given 1014.90. Whole-baseline fall-back: 781.60, which differs from the gold 1064.90. The one stamp-like field in this world, protection_plans.remaining_benefit_allowance = 1520.00, is stale by design (it still shows what was left in the second coverage year after the 2025 settlement and was never refreshed at the 2026-07-19 anniversary) and no rule reads it; the benefit standing is reconciled from the allowance entries instead.

FACTOR CARD, protection_ext_cancellation_refund (four declared factors, exactly the count drawn). coverage_run_basis (method, cross-difficulty on service): the work order carrying the reference of the claim last entered against the plan, initial_state.service_orders.3e2059dd-ed38-4f09-abca-627a3ca8d129, shows no date the piece was handed back and a promised date of 2026-09-25, later than the handling date, so the coverage keeps answering for the piece until it comes back and the whole months since the plan was bought are counted to that promised date, 26 rather than 25; the computation document counts them to the handling date and would have given 272.58. No field of any record carries 26, and the premium figures on the plan record play no part in this ladder. months_still_to_run (method): the most recent inspection is four whole months old against a six-month interval and the plan has run beyond its first coverage year, so the month in progress counts as still to run and ten months stand against a term of 36; the standard method drops the month in progress, giving nine months and 220.75. unused_premium_share (parameter): after the settlement lands, one settlement stands inside the twelve-month window and the benefit drawn in it, 1064.90, is below the heavy-draw share of the yearly allowance (0.5 times 2500.00 = 1250.00), so the light-claim share of 0.75 is returned; the baseline returns the whole unused premium and would have given 333.06. administration_fee_charged (parameter, cross-difficulty on circle): 790 calendar days have passed since the plan was bought, beyond the 30-day full-refund window, and the Gold tier carries a maintenance spend of 5000.00, so the fee is taken at the member share, 12.50 rather than 25.00; the baseline charges 25.00 and would have given 234.17. Whole-baseline fall-back: 320.56, which differs from the gold 246.67. The premium the customer has paid toward the plan is a plain reconciliation and no factor: the receipt of 1364.00 net of the give-back of 120.00 is 1244.00, which is also what the plan record's premium_paid_to_date carries, and no ladder's tier of this computation can be read off that or any other stored field.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The customer profile carries the three details the desk's identity check needs and the mailing address the cheque goes to. The plan row fixes the coverage held, the piece, the value at purchase (the ceiling), the term, the purchase date (every clock), the premium as sold and the stale displayed allowance. The twelve ledger rows are the reconciliation itself: the premium receipt and its give-back reconcile to the premium paid, 1244.00; the three allowance entries decide what benefit stands, only the 2026-07-19 reinstatement falling inside the twelve-month window so that the standing benefit is 2500.00; the four inspection entries decide both the wear rate (the latest records 'pass') and the months-still-to-run method (four whole months against a six-month interval), and the 2025-11-08 entry recording prong wear is there so that 'the most recent inspection' has to be read by date rather than by picking any inspection; the earlier filing and settlement under CL-320411 are the near-miss for the twelve-month settlement window and the excluded object for every claim-scoped read; the open filing under CL-320742 is the prerequisite itself. Remove the give-back and the refund is worked out on 1364.00 instead of 1244.00; remove the 2026 reinstatement and the settlement is capped at zero standing benefit; remove the open filing and there is no prerequisite and no claim reference to settle. The workshop rows are the cross-difficulty evidence: the live work order decides the figure standing for the repair, the service level decides the answered share and the rework test, and the old delivered order with its three lines is the distractor the claim reference excludes; the live order's empty handed-back date and its promised date of 2026-09-25 also decide how far the coverage is treated as having run when it is given up. The membership row decides the loyalty discount and the administration-fee share. Automatic clauses checked against the seed: no premium is owed (single payment, fully received), no inspection is overdue (next due 2026-11-12, after frozen time), the term has not run out (expiry 2027-07-18), the allowance is not consumed, and the coverage's minimum interval between settlements of 45 days and its cap of three settlements in a rolling twelve months are both satisfied, so no obligation is lit that this task does not discharge.

PERSONA DESIGN. Renata is written as a brisk, practical woman with a deadline, a move abroad on the sixth of October, rather than a grievance; the voice is short sentences and plain statements. She volunteers only the surface goal and the move; her identity details, her email, the whereabouts of the ring and her check-up history come only when asked; the one thing she is firm about is the cheque, which is the only customer-stated value any gold argument takes. Her passive reactions are tied to utterance events the agent produces, being told something must be dealt with on the ring first, being told the bench work is covered, being given the amount coming back, never to the state of the database. The natural trap is hers: the app has been showing about fifteen hundred of cover left, which is the stale displayed figure, and she asks whether that is what it was worked out from without offering a figure of her own. Her guess of something nearer five hundred is wrong and nothing uses it.

THE DEPENDENCY, LONG AND BROAD. Long: the surface goal (close the plan, return the unused premium) leads to the root policy's own rule, which says the premium returned is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the plan stands recorded against it; the ledger shows a claim entered on 2026-08-28 with no outcome; the settlement policy says what such a claim draws and books it; only then is the world in which the refund is computed the right one. Broad: the refund alone reads the premium entries and their give-backs, the inspection entries, the settlement entries inside a twelve-month window, the plan's term and purchase date and the loyalty tier's maintenance spend; the settlement alone reads the workshop's work order, its priced lines, its service level, the membership's standing and spend, the inspection findings and the allowance entries. Remove any one of them and a number moves.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Reading the displayed remaining allowance of 1520.00 instead of reconciling the allowance entries: the rule says the benefit still standing is the allowance granted and reinstated in the window less the settlements booked in it. Counting the September 2025 settlement as inside the twelve-month window: it is exactly twelve whole months back, and inside the window means fewer than twelve whole months. Taking the labour and parts already booked as the figure standing for the repair while the bench is still working and a ceiling stands. Taking the premium as sold rather than net of the give-back. Counting the months the plan has run to the handling date while the ring still stands at the bench under the claim with a promised date ahead, 25 instead of 26. Dropping the month in progress on a plan that has run beyond its first coverage year. Settling the claim after the cancellation, which would leave the refund computed on a world where no benefit stands recorded.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the customer by her mobile and verify her; read the coverage, its whole ledger, the workshop's orders and lines and the membership; see the claim entered on 2026-08-28 without an outcome; work the settlement out (1325.00 ceiling, less the 5 per cent loyalty discount giving 1258.75, less two years of wear at the sound-piece rate of 3.0 per cent giving 1183.225, at the expedited-level share of 0.9 giving 1064.9025, no deductible, under both the 12400.00 value ceiling and the 2500.00 benefit standing) and book 1064.90 with 0.00 out of pocket against CL-320742; then work the refund out on the world that leaves (1244.00 paid net, the months run counted to the ring's promised return date, 26, so ten months of 36 still to run, the light-claim share of 0.75, less the member share of the administration fee, 12.50) and hand the cancellation to the customer to confirm at 246.67, paid by cheque.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The two computations were evaluated with the gate's own evaluator (skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py, build_env and eval_compute) on the handling-time worlds: initial_state for the settlement, and initial_state plus the replayed settlement write for the refund. Output: protection_ext_claim_settlement result=1064.9 (29 bindings, 24 branches); per-factor baselines 759.5, 1120.95, 996.93, 1183.22, 1014.9; whole baseline 781.6. protection_ext_cancellation_refund result=246.67 (19 bindings, 13 branches); per-factor baselines 272.58 (coverage_run_basis), 220.75, 333.06, 234.17; whole baseline 320.56. Prerequisite sensitivity, same evaluator with the settlement write skipped: refund 333.06 against gold 246.67. Every figure recorded in computations and in this dossier is one of those outputs.

REWORK, ROUND 2 (audit revision_1). F-7 / F-0: the premium-paid-basis factor was removed, because its two non-fall-through tiers restated the premium account balance the plan record carries, and replaced by coverage_run_basis, which decides how far the coverage is treated as having run from the workshop's own record (the piece not handed back, the promised date ahead); the premium paid is now a plain reconciliation claimed by no factor. F-1: the base sentence on the full-refund window and the day the cancellation takes effect is now named in the overwrite and replaced by the rule's own in-window sentence. F-2: the pooling policy's coverage-year window is now named in protection_ext_claim_settlement's overwrite and replaced by the rule's own window sentence. O-1: the settlement rule now says that settlements stand as movements out of the allowance and the benefit consumed is read as their size. The refund gold moved from 272.58 to 246.67; the settlement is unchanged at 1064.90; every figure above is the round-2 recomputation.

CLOSURE. policy to tool to computation to gold call to terminal state: protection_ext_claim_settlement, record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c, computations[0] (arg benefit_amount, step 8), a protection_claim_settled entry of -1064.90 under CL-320742 with the plan's settled count at 2; protection_ext_cancellation_refund, confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509, computations[1] (arg refund_amount, step 10), the plan closed as cancelled on 2026-09-17 with a confirmed cancellation on the desk's request record and a premium-returned entry of -246.67. charter_scope, required_documents and the computations name the same two policies in the same order, and the task tools are exactly the two the gold calls, in first-use order.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Working only from what a rollout can see, the two coverage rules as they will be published, the two tool schemas, what the share tools return and what Renata actually says, the same conclusion follows: she is asking for the plan to be ended and the unused premium returned; the refund rule itself says the figure is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the plan stands recorded against it; the ledger shows exactly one claim without an outcome; the settlement rule gives a single figure for it from the work order carrying its reference; and the refund rule then gives a single figure from the premium entries, the term, the claims window and the membership. No second reading of either rule produces another number: each ladder's tiers are disjoint as stated, and every quantity they read is a record the share tools return.
user_scenario:
Renata Villalobos is fifty-five, an architect for a Chicago school district, unhurried on the telephone but plainly wanting this finished today rather than sometime next week. She and her husband move to Lisbon on the sixth of October and she is closing out everything she holds with Belrose before they go. She rings the protection desk about the care plan she bought in 2024 alongside her platinum engagement ring, and what she wants is simple: she wants to end the plan and get back whatever part of it she has not used. She puts it in exactly those words, has no idea how such a figure is worked out, and does not ask for a breakdown unless she is given a number first.

She gives her name at once. If the desk needs something to find her by she reads out her mobile, 3125553247, and if more is wanted she gives her date of birth, 1971-04-09, and the postal code on the account, 60614. Her email, r.villalobos@northbranchmail.com, is on a card in her bag and she will read it out if asked. She has no reference numbers of any kind in front of her, no plan number, no receipt and no claim number, and if she is asked for one she says so and asks the desk to find it from her name.

She is content for the agent to do whatever the account needs on her behalf, putting it as you sort it out, I just want it closed, with one thing she is firm about: whatever money comes back should go out as a cheque to the address on file, because the card she paid on was closed last year. Where the agent hands her something to confirm in her own name, she does it there and then and reads back whatever the confirmation returns to her.

Only if she is asked does she say where the ring actually is: she left it at the Lincoln Park store at the end of August because the centre stone had worked loose again, and it has not come back yet. Only if she is asked does she say that she has kept up the check-ups on it, the last one in the spring. She volunteers nothing about anything outstanding on the plan, because she has never thought about it and would not know where to look.

If the agent tells her something has to be dealt with on the ring before the plan can be closed, she does not argue: she says to go ahead and do whatever is needed, and waits. If the agent tells her the bench work on the ring has been covered, she is glad and says so, and only then does she mention that the Belrose app has been showing about fifteen hundred of cover left on the plan, asking whether that is the figure it was worked out from, without offering any view of her own about what it should be.

When she is finally given the amount coming back to her she is a little disappointed and says she had imagined something nearer five hundred, but she does not press a number of her own and accepts what she is told once it is explained. She confirms the cancellation herself when it is handed to her, and once she hears the plan is closed and the cheque is on its way she thanks the agent warmly, says something about the move, and rings off with nothing further to ask.

seed_consistency.check: The Belrose Care Plan 3-Year was written on a piece sold at 12400.00, between that coverage's smallest and largest admissible item values of 499.00 and 19999.00; the premium of 1364.00 is 11.0 per cent of that value; the plan was bought on the day of sale, inside the 30-day purchase window; the waiting period is zero, so coverage began the same day and the 36-month term runs to 2027-07-18; the value is below the 7499.00 above which this coverage requires an appraisal on file.

The premium receipt of 1364.00 on 2024-07-19 is the coverage's own price, 11.0 per cent of the item value of 12400.00 for a Belrose Care Plan 3-Year, collected in one payment on the day the plan was bought, as that coverage's premium schedule requires.

The give-back of -120.00 on 2024-08-06 is booked against the premium receipt through source_entry_id, is smaller than it, and leaves premium_paid_to_date at 1244.00, so the plan's premium account and its entries agree.
The allowance of 2500.00 granted on the effective date is exactly the coverage's yearly benefit allowance and is booked while the plan stands active, as the grant rule requires.
The reinstatement of 2500.00 on 2025-07-19 falls on the first anniversary of the effective date, which is what this coverage's annual reinstatement provides for.

The reinstatement of 2500.00 on 2026-07-19 falls on the second anniversary and is the grant for the coverage year in progress at frozen time; with the earlier grants it keeps the lifetime ceiling of 7500.00 for this coverage exactly met and never passed.
The inspection of 2024-11-21 at BR-118 falls within six whole months of the effective date, on a channel this coverage recognises, the customer's home store, and records a pass.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the caller's own customer profile from the mobile number she reads out, and read back the profile details the identity check will be measured against.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account can be reached without the customer reference this returns, and it is where the date of birth and postal code she states are checked against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Measure the two details the caller states against the profile on file and record that she cleared the check.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must stand before any record of hers is read or written, and two agreeing details are what the desk's check requires.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the coverage she holds: the plan variant, its status, the covered piece, the value it was sold at, the dates it runs between, the premium and what has been paid toward it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Fixes the coverage whose parameters every figure rests on, the term, the purchase date, the premium as sold, the piece, and the plan reference both writes are booked against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole coverage history: the premium received and given back, the allowance granted and reinstated, the inspections with their findings, and every claim filed, settled or refused.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: This is the reconciliation itself: the claim standing without an outcome, the benefit still standing, the settlement window, the inspection dates and findings, and the premium entries the refund is worked out on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the workshop's work orders for this customer, including the one carrying the claim's reference with its service level, its authorised ceiling, its estimate, its rework count and whether the bench has finished.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The figure standing for the repair, the share the coverage answers for and the wear reduction all rest on the work order carrying the claim reference.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the priced lines booked to those work orders, each carrying the protection claim reference it was raised under.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The labour and parts charged under the claim's reference are the standard method's figure for the repair and the check on what the authorised ceiling covers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's loyalty membership: its tier, whether it stands in force, and the qualifying spend recorded since the tier took effect.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The membership decides the loyalty discount taken off the figure standing for the repair and the share of the administration fee charged on the cancellation.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's own tool for answering a claim that stands open on a piece of coverage.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Answer the claim standing open on the ring: book the benefit it draws against the plan's allowance under its own claim reference and record what the customer bears out of pocket.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: protection_ext_claim_settlement is the only rule producing benefit_amount, and its result is what this write books; until it lands no benefit consumed stands recorded against the claim.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.protection_plan_id: The coverage record da7ae772-e1c5-4d1f-8ce9-100724b6f0dc. Basis: the protection coverage lookup returns exactly one coverage record for this customer, on the covered piece RING-32417 the claim names, and the tool schema says this argument is 'the reference number of the coverage record the claim stands against, as returned by the protection coverage lookup'. Uniqueness: the customer holds one coverage record, so no other value is reachable or correct.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_reference: CL-320742. Basis: the coverage history carries it on the filing entry of 2026-08-28, and the settlement rule says 'The claim being answered is the one last entered against the plan, and the work order it was sent in on is the one carrying that claim's reference.' Uniqueness: two claim references appear in the ledger, CL-320411 and CL-320742; the first already carries a settlement of 2025-09-02 and is answered, and the base rule 'A settlement is made only when no settlement already stands against that same claim reference' excludes it, so only CL-320742 remains.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_entry_id: The coverage entry b803ba2d-26a7-411f-8f38-5589c47c6b87. Basis: the tool schema says this is 'the reference number of the coverage entry on which the loss was first entered, as returned by the coverage history lookup; the settlement is recorded as the answer to that entry'. Uniqueness: exactly one entry in the ledger carries claim_reference CL-320742 with event_type protection_claim_filed, and it is that one.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_amount: 1064.90, the value protection_ext_claim_settlement computes on the world at this step. The claim last entered is CL-320742 and the work order carrying that reference is WO-321065, which shows no date the bench finished the work and an authorised ceiling of 1325.00 above zero, so the figure standing for the repair is 1325.00 rather than the 945.00 of labour and parts so far booked or the 1180.00 estimate. The membership stands active with qualifying spend of 8420.00 since the tier took effect against the Gold maintenance figure of 5000.00, so the whole of the Master Jeweler Service loyalty discount of 5 per cent comes off once, giving 1258.75, which is the base every later step acts on. The piece was sold on 2024-07-19 and the handling date is 2026-09-17, so two whole years of wear have run; the most recent inspection entry, 2026-05-12, records the piece sound and the work order records no rework, so the annual reduction is the sound-piece share of the coverage's 6.0 per cent, that is 3.0 per cent a year, and 1258.75 times (1 - 0.06) is 1183.225. The service level targets 10 business days against the coverage's own 12 and the coverage offers expedited handling, so the coverage answers for the expedited-level share, 1183.225 times 0.9 giving 1064.9025. No settlement entry falls inside the twelve-month window (the earlier settlement of 2025-09-02 is exactly twelve whole months back, and so outside it) and the most recent inspection is four whole months old against a six-month interval, so nothing is charged to the customer. 1064.9025 is below both the value ceiling (12400.00 at 100 per cent) and the benefit standing (the 2026-07-19 reinstatement of 2500.00, with no settlement booked in the window), and rounds once at the end to 1064.90. Any agent reading the same rule off the same records converges on it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.deductible_charged: 0.00, the deductible this claim bears under the same rule. Basis: 'Where no settlement stands against the plan in the window the coverage counts settlements over and the most recent inspection was logged within the coverage's inspection interval, nothing is charged to the customer.' Uniqueness: the only settlement in the ledger is dated 2025-09-02, exactly twelve whole months before the handling date and therefore outside the window, and the most recent inspection of 2026-05-12 is four whole months old against a six-month interval, so the first tier of that ladder is the only one whose condition holds, and the tool schema requires the value in USD to two decimal places, that is 0.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's own cancellation confirmation and hand it over to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Ending cover she paid for is hers alone to do, so the desk unlocks the confirmation rather than performing it; the unlock changes nothing.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The customer confirms the cancellation herself: the coverage closes as cancelled today, the cancellation is recorded as confirmed on the desk's request record, and the premium due goes back to her by cheque.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: protection_ext_cancellation_refund is the only rule producing refund_amount, and it is evaluated on the world the settlement has already changed; the confirmation is the customer's own write.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.protection_plan_id: The coverage record da7ae772-e1c5-4d1f-8ce9-100724b6f0dc, the same coverage the claim was answered on. Basis: the tool schema says this argument is 'the reference number of the coverage record being given up, as returned by the protection coverage lookup'. Uniqueness: the customer holds exactly one coverage record and it is the one her request is about.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount: 246.67, the value protection_ext_cancellation_refund computes on the world at this step. The premium she has paid toward the plan is the receipt of 1364.00 net of the give-back of -120.00 booked against it, 1244.00. The work order carrying the reference of the claim last entered against the plan, WO-321065, shows no date the ring was handed back and a promised date of 2026-09-25, later than the handling date, so the coverage keeps answering for the ring until it comes back and the whole months since the plan was bought on 2024-07-19 are counted to that date, 26. The most recent inspection entry of 2026-05-12 is four whole months old against a six-month interval and the plan has run beyond its first coverage year, so the month in progress counts as still to run and ten of the 36 months of the term stand still to run. A settlement now stands inside the twelve-month claims window and the benefit drawn in it, 1064.90, is below the heavy-draw share of the yearly allowance (0.5 of 2500.00, that is 1250.00), so the light-claim share of 0.75 of the unused premium is returned. 790 calendar days have passed since the plan was bought, beyond the 30-day full-refund window, and the membership tier carries a maintenance spend of 5000.00, so the administration fee is charged at the member share, 12.50. 1244.00 times 10/36 times 0.75 is 259.1666..., less 12.50, which rounds once at the end to 246.67.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_channel: mail_check. Basis: the customer says 'whatever money comes back should go out as a cheque to the address on file, because the card she paid on was closed last year', and the tool schema defines mail_check as the value to pass 'where a cheque is posted to the address on the profile'. Uniqueness: in_store is excluded because she is on the telephone and about to move abroad, online_portal and phone_agent are excluded because the card she paid on is closed, autopay is excluded because a single-payment plan has no standing arrangement to credit, and not_applicable is excluded because money does move to her.

edges.condition: every claim entered against the plan carries a settlement entry booked under its own claim reference recording the benefit it consumed
edges.policy_source: The premium returned is fixed only after the benefit consumed by every claim entered against the plan stands recorded against it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The claim entered against the plan on 2026-08-28 under CL-320742 stands with no outcome at all: no settlement entry anywhere in the coverage's history carries that claim reference, so no benefit consumed stands recorded against it and the state the refund waits on does not hold.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The settlement written at step 8 books a protection_claim_settled entry under CL-320742 for -1064.90 with claim_outcome settled_full, so the benefit consumed then stands recorded against every claim entered against the plan, and the refund's returned_share binding moves from the whole unused premium, 1.0, to the light-claim share, 0.75, and refund_amount from 333.06 to 246.67.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain with one edge, so no two writes can be reordered: the settlement precedes the cancellation and there is no pair of parallel prerequisites whose order could be swapped. The order is not a convention either: the refund's own rule fixes the figure only after the benefit consumed by every claim stands recorded, and running the cancellation first would compute the refund on a world where no settlement stands in the claims window, giving 333.06 instead of 246.67 and a different terminal hash.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the settlement write and replaying everything else leaves settlements_in_window at 0 and benefit_drawn_window at 0.00, so returned_share takes the fall-through tier of 1.0 and refund_amount moves from 246.67 to 333.06; the terminal state also loses the protection_claim_settled entry and the plan's claims_settled_count stays at 1 instead of 2.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario names neither the prerequisite problem nor what it resolves. Renata asks only to end the plan and get back what she has not used; she never mentions a claim, a settlement, an outstanding item or anything that must be sorted first, and she asks no leading question. That the ring is at the Lincoln Park store is stated only if the agent asks where the piece is, and says nothing about a claim standing unanswered. Her only contributions about the prerequisite are passive: after the agent tells her something must be dealt with on the ring first she says to go ahead, and after the agent tells her the bench work has been covered she mentions the figure her app displays.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_plan_cancellation_48603509 never looks at any claim: its body reads the plan row and the plan's premium entries, writes the request record, the premium-returned entry and the plan's closing fields, and returns a confirmation line. It has no branch that inspects claim_outcome, raises an error or refuses, so with the settlement unresolved it would still write a cancellation and a refund of whatever amount it was given, and only the terminal hash would differ. record_claim_settlement_8eb9093c likewise checks nothing about the cancellation and would write at any time.
